questions.q: Why does this lesson scale FeedbackScope on concurrent requests per instance instead of CPU?
options: CPU metrics are not available for CPU-only models
Concurrency-based scaling is the only option any cloud platform supports
It's a more direct measure of whether an instance is keeping up, and generalizes to a future, bigger model
CPU-based scaling is always slower to configure
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly picks concurrency because it's a more direct load signal and the same approach would still work if the model later needed a GPU.

questions.q: Why is FeedbackScope's min_instances set to 1 rather than higher?
options: Because the platform does not allow a higher minimum
Because autoscaling is disabled for this service
Because the model never needs to be reloaded
Because this app's cold start is genuinely short on CPU, making a low floor tolerable
questions.explain: Unlike a GPU-backed model with a multi-minute cold start, this CPU-only model starts in 1-2 seconds, so a low min is a reasonable, justified choice here.

questions.q: Why is max_instances capped at 5 in this capstone's policy?
options: As a hard ceiling on cost, since this is a portfolio project without a production budget
Because 5 is the maximum any cloud provider allows
Because higher counts would exceed the model's accuracy limits
Because the health check only supports 5 concurrent instances
questions.explain: Max instances here is explicitly a cost ceiling appropriate for a learning project's real but small cloud bill.

questions.q: What makes this lesson's health check more meaningful than one that only confirms the process is running?
options: It checks the Dockerfile for syntax errors
It measures GPU temperature before responding
It counts the number of instances currently running
It actually loads a test sentence through the model and only returns 200 if the model returns a real result
questions.explain: A liveness-only check would pass even with a broken model load -- this one exercises the model itself, catching that failure mode.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say FeedbackScope skips semantic caching, unlike a FAQ bot?
options: Semantic caching is technically impossible for sentiment-analysis models
FeedbackScope's inputs are short and highly varied, with a low repeat rate, so a semantic cache would rarely hit
FeedbackScope does not use any machine learning model
Caching is only available for GPU-backed services
questions.explain: Lesson 19's point was that caching isn't automatically right for every app -- FeedbackScope's varied, low-repeat traffic is exactly the case where it isn't worth the complexity.
